title: Data Sufficiency Mastery
tagline: Year 4 — All four outcomes with numbers, percentages, ratios and yes/no questions; a quick decision procedure

introduction.overview: Data sufficiency asks whether given statements are enough to answer a question. Mastery means deciding quickly and correctly in all four outcomes: I alone, II alone, both together, neither. The procedure is the same each time: list the unknowns, test statement I alone by trying to find two different answers, test II the same way, and combine only if both fail. For yes/no questions the answer must be always yes or always no.
introduction.placementRelevance: Data sufficiency is common in management-oriented tests and in the advanced DI and reasoning sections.
introduction.realWorldContext: Deciding whether you have enough information before committing to a decision is the real-world skill.

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A statement is sufficient only if it leads to a single answer in every situation it allows.

coreDefinitions: Insufficient: more than one answer possible.
Consistent yes/no: always yes or always no.
Redundant: adds nothing to the other.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Picture every situation the statement permits. If they all agree, it suffices.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Try to build two worlds with different answers for I; then for II; then for I and II together.

mainNarrative: Company A sold ₹40 lakh and B sold 25% more: B sold 50, total 90. "B sold more than 45" leaves 46, 47, …; only I is sufficient.
"x² > y²" for positive whole numbers means x > y, so it settles "is x greater than y?"; "x + y = 10" does not.
"n is divisible by 12" leaves 12, 24, 36, 48; "n is divisible by 18" leaves 18, 36; together n = 36.
A rectangle with perimeter 24 has l + w = 12; area 36 gives l = w = 6 only when both hold: together they show a square.
Where a yes/no answer varies across the permitted worlds, the statement is insufficient.

deepDiveAspects.title: Hidden constraints
deepDiveAspects.content: Check the ranges in the setup: they can make a statement sufficient.

deepDiveAspects.title: Both together but not enough
deepDiveAspects.content: Two statements can overlap so much that they still leave several possibilities.

solvedExamples.title: I alone
solvedExamples.question: A sold ₹40 lakh. I. B sold 25% more than A. II. B sold more than ₹45 lakh. Total of A and B?
solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not

solvedExamples.title: Both needed
solvedExamples.question: n ≤ 50. I. n is divisible by 12. II. n is divisible by 18. What is n?
solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient

solvedExamples.title: Yes/no
solvedExamples.question: x, y positive whole numbers. I. x² > y². Is x > y?

steps.title: Squares
steps.explanation: For positive numbers x² > y² means x > y.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Try to find two different answers under I, then under II, then under both.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: If statements repeat, together adds nothing.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: You never need the exact answer.
